memory_candidates.content: When a plan's final phase requires a redeploy (source store -> deployed .claude/ tree) and earlier phases must verify source-store-only changes before that redeploy runs, use the test harness's own CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store environment override (scripts/lib/common.sh's common_test_resolve_subject) to point suite runs at the source-store copy instead of the stale deployed one. Do NOT set this override globally when running run-all.sh alongside test-common-lib.sh in the same invocation -- that suite's own fixtures assert the DEFAULT deploy-tree-first resolution behavior, and the override corrupts them into a false failure. Run test-common-lib.sh separately, unmodified, when it is part of a named covering-check set.

To distinguish a real regression from a transient full-battery concurrency flake in this repo's gate (verify-deploy.sh / run-all.sh): (1) check whether the failing suite is tagged (EXPECTED) vs (NEW) in run-all.sh's own output -- EXPECTED means it is pre-registered in known-failures.txt and is a standing, repo-wide condition unrelated to any one task; (2) for a NEW failure, re-run that one suite in isolation immediately -- if it passes cleanly, and the full-battery run showed a 'WARN: reclaiming stale specs/.gate-lock mutex' or similar concurrency signal nearby, the failure is very likely a resource-contention flake, not a regression, especially when the failing suite's domain has no relationship to the files the task actually touched. run-all.sh's own exit-code semantics mark exit 1 on ANY suite failure (EXPECTED or not) unless --fail-on-new is passed, so an unqualified verify-deploy.sh pass can be structurally unattainable while a known-failures.txt entry stands, independent of any given task.
